title: AI Advisory Services Strategy
summary: How AOM turns its internal AI system into a sellable product.
content:
AI Advisory Market Research Brief

Prepared for: Patrik Matheson, AOM Date: 2026-03-10 Authors: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) + Alex (Strategy)

Executive Summary

The AI consulting market for small businesses is real, growing fast, and undeniably underserved. The global AI consulting market hit $11.4B in 2022 and is projected to reach $64.3B by 2028 (37.5% CAGR). But here's what matters for AOM: the "brutal mid-market gap" between enterprise consultancies ($50k+ engagements) and DIY tools (ChatGPT, Zapier) is wide open. Small businesses with 5-50 employees know they need AI but have no idea how to implement it, no budget for McKinsey, and no time to figure it out themselves.

AOM's pricing instinct ($2,500 audit, $5-8k system build) lands right in the sweet spot. The market validates it. The competition is fragmented. And AOM has something almost nobody else does: a working multi-agent system running a real business.

Verdict: The opportunity is real. Move on it.

1. Market Overview

Market Size and Growth

  • Global AI consulting services: $11.4B (2022), projected $64.3B by 2028
  • AI marketplace overall: $390.9B in 2025, 35.9% CAGR through 2030
  • 84% of companies plan to increase AI investments in the next year
  • 74% of organizations report meeting or exceeding expected ROI from AI initiatives

The SMB Gap

Small and mid-market companies sit in what analysts call the "brutal mid-market gap":

  • Big consultancy fees are too high for their budgets
  • Off-the-shelf tools cap out quickly
  • They lack internal knowledge to form an AI implementation strategy
  • They're "primed to benefit" but have no path to get there

This is AOM's lane.

SMB Spending Patterns

  • Most SMBs spend $10,000-$50,000 on initial AI projects
  • Basic AI readiness assessments: $2,000-$8,000
  • Strategy + roadmap: $8,000-$25,000
  • Pilot implementation (1-2 use cases): $15,000-$50,000
  • Monthly retainers for ongoing advisory: $1,000-$7,000/month
  • Breakeven timeline: months 2-3, with 200%+ ROI by months 4-6

The Construction Vertical Specifically

This is critical for AOM since construction is the target vertical:

  • 6+ million people employed in U.S. specialty trades
  • Small/mid-sized trade contractors are driving the fastest growth in software adoption
  • HVAC, plumbing, and electrical contractors are among the first early adopters of AI in real business applications
  • Top use cases: estimating/bidding automation, admin automation, document management, invoice processing, project reporting
  • AI tools for construction can automate takeoffs and generate cost estimates in minutes instead of hours
  • The vertical is massively underserved by serious AI consulting

Bottom line: AOM already targets construction companies for social media. Adding AI operations consulting to the same clients is a natural upsell.

2. Competitor Profiles

Tier 1: Direct Competitors (SMB-focused AI consulting)

AI SMB Solutions (aismbsolutions.com)

  • What they offer: AI Opportunity Blueprint, org chart overlay, tool matrix, custom GPT creation (3-10 GPTs), prompt packages, white-glove implementation
  • Pricing: Not public. "AI Opportunity Blueprint" is their lead product
  • Differentiator: They audit by role and department, mapping AI opportunities across the org
  • Threat to AOM: Medium. Similar positioning but no multi-agent system. More template-driven.

Authority AI (authorityai.ai) -- Fort Lauderdale, FL

  • What they offer: AI bots, AI-powered CRM, custom AI estimators, document generators, internal knowledge bots
  • Target: Law firms, insurance agencies, trade businesses, medical practices
  • Pricing: Free initial consultation, custom pricing after
  • Differentiator: They explicitly target trade businesses (overlap with AOM's construction vertical)
  • Threat to AOM: Medium-high for construction clients. They're in the same market.

Suns Out Agency (sunsout.agency) -- Seattle

  • What they offer: AI readiness audits, workflow automation, custom GPT development, team training. Also traditional services (content strategy, digital marketing)
  • Pricing: Not public
  • Differentiator: Blend of traditional agency + AI consulting. Closest model to what AOM would be.
  • Threat to AOM: Low-medium. Different geography, similar hybrid model.

Opinosis Analytics (opinosis-analytics.com) -- Founded by Dr. Kavita Ganesan

  • What they offer: Full-cycle AI consulting from strategy through implementation. 20+ years experience.
  • Clients: 3M, Microsoft, eBay, McKesson, federal agencies
  • Pricing: "Competitive," claims ROI within 3-6 months
  • Differentiator: Deep technical expertise, academic credentials
  • Threat to AOM: Low. Enterprise-leaning despite SMB messaging.

Vstorm (vstorm.co) -- Poland/UK/Germany

  • What they offer: Agentic AI consultation, custom RAG implementations, workflow automation for SMBs
  • Pricing: Projects starting ~$3,500. Recognized by Deloitte and EY.
  • Differentiator: Boutique, budget-friendly, agentic AI focus
  • Threat to AOM: Low. Different geography (EU-based), but their pricing validates AOM's range.

Xcelacore (xcelacore.com) -- Chicago

  • What they offer: AI strategy development, Microsoft Copilot integration, process automation, generative AI for meetings/data/personalization
  • Pricing: Flexible: time-and-materials, fixed-price, or outcome-based
  • Differentiator: Ranked #1 for mid-size orgs due to agile methodology and cost efficiency
  • Threat to AOM: Low-medium. More tech/enterprise leaning.

Tier 2: Construction-Specific AI Players

Estes Media (estesmedia.com)

  • What they offer: AI consulting specifically for contractors, builders, architects. Free "AI Readiness & Opportunity Assessment" call (30 min). Help evaluate AI tools for lead gen, email outreach, chatbots, voice assistants.
  • Pricing: Not public for AI consulting. Digital marketing pricing visible.
  • Differentiator: They explicitly serve contractors. Very close to AOM's territory.
  • Threat to AOM: High. They're already selling AI consulting to contractors.

ContractorGX (contractorgx.com)

  • What they offer: AI-powered marketing automation, PPC, SEO, conversion-optimized websites for HVAC, roofing, plumbing, electrical contractors
  • Pricing: AI-adjacent, more marketing automation than true AI ops consulting
  • Differentiator: Verticalized for contractors
  • Threat to AOM: Medium. More marketing than operations, but in the same client base.

The Contractor AI Suite (thecontractor.ai)

  • What they offer: 7 AI-powered tools for $47 total: scheduling, social media, customer support, copywriting, sales, image generation, reminders
  • Pricing: $47 (one-time or low monthly)
  • Differentiator: Dirt cheap, self-serve
  • Threat to AOM: Low. This is DIY, not consulting. But it's what uninformed contractors might try first.

Tier 3: Fractional AI Officer Services

Momentum AI -- Fractional CAIO starting at $2,500/month GAI Insights (gaiinsights.com) -- Fractional CAIO services AI First Mindset (aifirstmindset.ai) -- Fractional CAIO Head of AI (headofai.ai) -- Marketplace of fractional CAIOs for hire

  • Pricing range: $2,500-$30,000/month depending on scope
  • Note: These are typically senior individual consultants, not agencies. They sell time, not systems.

Tier 4: DIY / Self-Serve (what AOM competes against)

Zapier -- $20-$100/month. 7,000+ integrations. No-code automation. Make (make.com) -- $9-$145/month. More powerful than Zapier, cheaper at scale. n8n -- Self-hosted option, execution-based billing. Most technical of the three. ChatGPT / Claude -- Direct AI access for $20-$200/month per user.

These aren't competitors in the consulting sense. They're the "I'll figure it out myself" option. The problem: most small business owners try these, get overwhelmed, and give up. That's AOM's entry point.

3. Gap Analysis: Where AOM Fits

What exists today:

  1. Enterprise consultancies (McKinsey, BCG, Deloitte) -- $50k-$500k+. Not for SMBs.
  2. Fractional CAIOs -- $2.5k-$30k/month. Senior individuals selling time.
  3. SMB AI consulting agencies -- $2k-$50k projects. Growing but fragmented.
  4. DIY tools -- $20-$200/month. Accessible but overwhelming.
  5. Construction-specific AI marketing -- Estes Media, ContractorGX. Mostly marketing, not operations.

What's missing:

  • A creative agency that ALSO does AI operations. Everyone above is either a tech consultancy or a marketing agency. Nobody is both.
  • A proven, running multi-agent system as the case study. Every competitor talks about what they CAN build. AOM can show what it HAS built.
  • Verticalized AI ops for construction. Estes Media touches this but focuses on marketing tools, not operational systems (scheduling, estimating, project tracking, internal comms).
  • Ongoing management, not just builds. Most competitors sell a project and walk away. AOM's retainer model (already proven with social media) maps perfectly to ongoing AI ops management.

AOM's Unique Position:

  1. You are the case study. Multi-agent pipeline with QA gates, Telegram relay for mobile command, skills system for repeatable workflows. Nobody else has this. You're not selling theory.
  2. Creative + AI hybrid. AOM already does video, web, brand, social. Adding AI advisory means one vendor for the client instead of three.
  3. Construction vertical expertise. You already know these clients, their pain points, their budgets, their communication style.
  4. Retainer model. You're not selling a one-time audit and disappearing. You're selling ongoing AI operations management alongside social media management. One relationship, multiple revenue streams.

4. Pricing Strategy

Market-Validated Pricing Tiers

Based on all research, here's what the market supports:

Tier 1: AI Operations Audit -- $2,500

  • 2-3 hour discovery session (in-person or video)
  • Audit of current tools, workflows, communication patterns, time sinks
  • Deliverable: AI Opportunity Roadmap (prioritized list of AI use cases with estimated ROI)
  • Timeline: 1 week turnaround
  • Market comparison: $2,000-$8,000 range for similar assessments. $2,500 is competitive and accessible.

Tier 2: System Build -- $5,000-$8,000

  • Implementation of top 2-3 recommendations from the audit
  • Could include: AI-powered scheduling, automated invoicing, AI chatbot for customer inquiries, automated social posting, internal knowledge base
  • Training for the team (1-2 sessions)
  • 30-day post-launch support
  • Timeline: 2-4 weeks
  • Market comparison: $10,000-$50,000 for similar implementations. AOM is underpricing the market, which is actually a strength for construction clients who are price-sensitive.

Tier 3: Ongoing AI Operations Retainer -- $1,500-$3,000/month

  • Monthly optimization of AI systems
  • New automation builds as needs emerge
  • Monitoring, troubleshooting, updates
  • Monthly reporting on time saved / efficiency gained
  • Can bundle with existing social media retainer for a package deal
  • Market comparison: $1,000-$7,000/month. AOM's range is right in the sweet spot.

Bundle Play:

  • Social media retainer ($3k/month) + AI ops retainer ($2k/month) = $5k/month per client
  • 15 clients x $5k = $75k/month = $900k/year
  • Even 10 clients at the bundle rate = $600k/year

Pricing Psychology

  • $2,500 audit is low enough that a construction company owner says yes without a committee
  • The audit naturally leads to the system build (you're showing them what's broken)
  • The retainer naturally follows the build (who's going to maintain this?)
  • Value-based pricing (73% of clients now prefer outcome-based models): tie pricing to hours saved or revenue gained

5. Go-to-Market Recommendations

Phase 1: First 3 Clients (Weeks 1-4)

Sell to existing relationships first.

  • Ambition Mechanical is the obvious first candidate. You're already their vendor. Offer the audit at a discount or free as a case study.
  • Any other current or past AOM clients in construction.
  • Ash's network in the trades.

What you need before the first sale:

  1. A one-page service overview (not a full website page yet, just a PDF or landing page)
  2. Your own case study written up: "Here's how AOM runs on AI agents" with specific numbers (hours saved, tasks automated, response times)
  3. The audit framework: a repeatable questionnaire/discovery process that Steve or Alex can run
  4. A simple proposal template

What you do NOT need:

  • A perfect website page
  • A polished deck
  • Custom software
  • Certifications

Phase 2: Outreach (Weeks 4-8)

Jacob's outreach system is the channel.

  • Same construction vertical Jacob is already targeting for social media
  • New angle in the cold email: "We help construction companies automate their back office with AI"
  • LinkedIn content from Patrik: "Here's how I run my agency with AI agents" (this IS the thought leadership)
  • Local Phoenix construction events, trade shows, BNI groups

Key messaging:

  • "You know AI is important. You don't have time to figure it out. We did it for ourselves and now we do it for you."
  • "We saved X hours/week by automating Y. Here's what that could look like for your business."
  • Lead with the audit. It's a low-commitment entry point.

Phase 3: Scale (Months 3-6)

  • Build out the AI advisory page on aom-inhouse.com (Bobby + Steffen)
  • Document 2-3 client case studies with real ROI numbers
  • Consider a "Construction AI Playbook" as a lead magnet
  • Explore partnerships with construction software vendors (ServiceTitan, Buildertrend, Housecall Pro)
  • Tony posts about AI operations on LinkedIn consistently

Sales Channels (Ranked by Priority)

  1. Existing clients -- Easiest close. They already trust you.
  2. Jacob's cold outreach -- Same vertical, new offer. Add AI ops to the email sequences.
  3. LinkedIn (Patrik's personal brand) -- Share what you've built. Construction owners follow other construction-adjacent business owners.
  4. Local networking -- Phoenix construction events, trade associations, BNI
  5. Referrals -- After 2-3 happy clients, ask for introductions
  6. Website inbound -- Longer play but compounds over time

6. What to Build First (Minimum Viable Product)

The Audit Framework

This is the product. Not software. Not a platform. A structured process:

  1. Discovery questionnaire (30 questions covering):

    • Current tech stack (what software do you use daily?)
    • Communication patterns (email, phone, text, apps?)
    • Time sinks (what takes the most time every week?)
    • Pain points (what makes you want to throw your phone?)
    • Team structure (who does what, how do they coordinate?)
    • Data/document management (where does everything live?)

  2. Audit walkthrough (2-3 hours, on-site or video):

    • Watch how they actually work
    • Identify manual processes that could be automated
    • Map their workflow visually
    • Note what tools they're already paying for but underusing

  3. AI Opportunity Roadmap (deliverable):

    • Top 5-7 AI automation opportunities ranked by impact and ease
    • Estimated hours saved per week for each
    • Recommended tools/platforms for each
    • Implementation timeline
    • Investment required

The System Build Playbook

For each common construction use case, have a repeatable build:

  • Automated scheduling/dispatching -- AI-powered job assignment based on crew availability, location, skills
  • AI estimating assistant -- Feed it specs, get a draft estimate
  • Customer communication bot -- Automated appointment confirmations, follow-ups, review requests
  • Document management -- AI-organized project files, searchable by natural language
  • Invoice processing -- Auto-reconciliation, payment tracking, late payment alerts
  • Internal knowledge base -- "How do we handle X?" answered by AI trained on company SOPs

7. Positioning Against DIY Tools

The Objection: "Can't I just use ChatGPT?"

The answer:

  • ChatGPT is a tool. AOM builds a system.
  • ChatGPT answers one question at a time. AOM's approach connects your scheduling, your invoicing, your customer comms, your project tracking into one automated workflow.
  • Using ChatGPT for business is like having a really smart intern who forgets everything every day. AOM builds the intern a brain, a process, and makes it permanent.
  • Most business owners who try ChatGPT use it for 2 weeks and stop. They don't know what to ask, don't know how to integrate it, and don't have time to learn.
  • AOM has been running its entire operation on AI agents for months. The system works. We'll build you one that works too.

Against Zapier/Make:

  • "Zapier connects apps. We build intelligent workflows that think."
  • "You can connect your calendar to your email. We can build a system that reads a new project request, checks crew availability, drafts a response, schedules the site visit, and updates your project tracker -- without you touching anything."

8. Risks and Unknowns

Risks

  1. Delivery capacity. Patrik is one person. Audits take time. System builds take more. Until AOM hires or trains someone, this doesn't scale past 3-4 active builds.

    • Mitigation: Start with audits only (low time commitment, high margin). System builds come after you have cash flow from audit revenue.

  2. Client expectations. Small business owners may expect magic. AI is powerful but requires clean data, defined processes, and some behavior change.

    • Mitigation: The audit sets expectations. Be honest about what AI can and can't do. Underpromise, overdeliver.

  3. Market education. Some construction owners don't know they need this yet. Cold outreach may get "we don't need AI" responses.

    • Mitigation: Lead with pain points, not technology. "Are you spending 4 hours a week on scheduling?" not "Do you want an AI agent?"

  4. Competition heating up. This market is growing fast. More players will enter.

    • Mitigation: Move now. First-mover advantage in the Phoenix construction market matters. Build relationships before competitors show up.

  5. Tool/platform risk. AI tools change fast. What you build today might need rebuilding in 6 months.

    • Mitigation: This is actually a selling point for the retainer model. "AI moves fast. We keep your systems current."

Unknowns

  1. Willingness to pay. We have market data on pricing, but we don't have data on whether Phoenix construction companies specifically will pay $2,500 for an audit. First 3 sales will answer this.

  2. Repeat vs. one-time. Will clients convert from audit to build to retainer at the rates we project? Conversion funnel data doesn't exist yet.

  3. Ash's role. Does Ash want to co-sell this? Can Ash run audits independently? This determines scale.

  4. Legal/liability. If an AI system makes a mistake (wrong estimate, missed appointment), who's liable? Needs a basic service agreement with clear disclaimers.

  5. Case study permission. Can AOM publicly share results from client implementations? Need to ask for this upfront.

9. The Bottom Line

Why this works for AOM:

  • The market is validated. $2,000-$50,000 is the established range for SMB AI consulting. AOM's pricing fits.
  • The gap is real. Nobody is doing creative production + AI operations for construction companies. Zero.
  • The case study is built. AOM is already running on AI agents. That's the proof.
  • The sales channel exists. Jacob's outreach, Patrik's network, existing clients. No new infrastructure needed.
  • The economics stack. Audit ($2.5k) + Build ($5-8k) + Retainer ($2k/month) per client. 10 clients = serious revenue.
  • Industry specialists command 30-40% fee premiums over generalists. AOM as a construction-focused AI consultant charges more, not less.

What to do this week:

  1. Write the AOM case study (Steve can draft this)
  2. Build the audit questionnaire framework
  3. Pitch Ambition Mechanical as the first audit (free or discounted)
  4. Add AI advisory angle to Jacob's outreach copy
  5. Patrik posts on LinkedIn about running his business on AI agents

What to do this month:

  1. Complete first paid audit
  2. Draft the system explainer page content for aom-inhouse.com
  3. Create a simple proposal template
  4. Start building the Construction AI Playbook lead magnet
